title: T-Bill Cut-off Yields (91/182/364-day)
description: Cut-off (implicit) yield at the RBI's weekly Treasury bill auctions for the 91-, 182- and 364-day bills, per cent, dated by auction day. These are the clearest market read on short-term risk-free rates and liquidity expectations, moving ahead of policy changes and money-market stress. HISTORY IS SHORT: this series is recorded from RBI press releases as they appear, starting 2026-10-14, and grows with every weekly auction; it is not a full historical series.
source: Reserve Bank of India (T-bill auction result press releases)

qna.question: What is the T-bill cut-off yield?
qna.answer: At each weekly auction the RBI accepts bids from the lowest yield upward until the notified amount is filled; the highest accepted yield is the cut-off. The press release gives the cut-off price and the implied yield (YTM) for the 91-, 182- and 364-day bills.^It is a primary-market rate for risk-free government borrowing at three short maturities.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Yields track the expected policy repo rate and system liquidity: a surplus pulls them below the repo rate, a deficit pushes them up. A wider gap between 364-day and 91-day yields signals expectations of higher rates ahead.^Compare with the repo rate and the net LAF series elsewhere on the dashboard.

qna.question: Caveats?
qna.answer: The dashboard records each auction from the RBI press release as it is published, so history starts on 2026-10-14 and the series is short. Do not read it as a long-run record.^Occasionally the RBI rejects all bids or the auction is not held; the release then shows NA and no point is recorded for that week.

note: Accumulating series: history starts 2026-10-14 and grows with each run. Auctions where RBI reports no cut-off (all bids rejected, shown as NA) leave a gap.
